title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study semi-simplicial modules L (face maps only, no degeneracies) over a principal ideal ring k that are '∂-perfect' or '∂-projective', meaning their associated chain complexes are perfect. The aim is to classify them up to isomorphism by numerical and homological invariants.

Previous page. Grothendieck splits the normalized chain complex of such an object over a PID. It decomposes into three kinds of pieces:
- free modules N_i[-i] with zero differential (the free part of homology);
- contractible pieces;
- two-term pieces k --n--> k with n ≠ 0, given by elementary-divisor theory.

This page. For each such two-term piece he introduces an indecomposable semi-simplicial module L(i,n). It is the object associated to the complex 0 → k --n--> k → 0, sitting in degrees i and i-1 (he writes i, i+1). It depends only on the ideal div(n) = l, which is why he also writes L(i,l).

It fits into an extension 0 → Λ^{i-1}Ψ → L(i,n) → Λ^iΨ → 0. Here Ψ is presumably the reduced standard semi-simplicial module, with Ψ_m of rank m, so Λ^jΨ has rank C(m,j) and homology k concentrated in degree j. The map k → k induced on the associated homology (the connecting map) is n·id. Hence:
- H_j(L(i,n)) = 0 for j ≠ i-1;
- H_{i-1}(L(i,n)) = k/(n), a torsion module.

Remark 1 (Hilbert functions). The rank of L(i,n) in simplicial degree m is C(m,i-1) + C(m,i) = C(m+1,i). This equals the rank of Λ^iL, where L is the standard module with L_m = k^{m+1} (free on the vertices of Δ^m), so Λ^iL_m has the rank of the (i-1)-faces. So the Hilbert function of L(i,n) cannot be told apart from that of the (acyclic) Λ^iL.

Rank formula. For a ∂-perfect L, which is a direct sum of indecomposables Λ^iL (multiplicity μ_i), L(i,·) (ρ_i of them) and Λ^jΨ (ν_j of them):

rg L_m = Σ_i (μ_i + ρ_i) C(m+1,i) + Σ_j ν_j C(m,j).

Conclusion. L is known up to isomorphism once one knows:
- (a) the homology: ranks ν_i of H_i(L), and the torsion divisors of H_i(L), whose number is ρ_{i+1};
- (b) the Hilbert function m ↦ rg L_m for m large, which agrees with the polynomial above.

From (b) one subtracts the ν and ρ contributions and reads off the μ_i, since the binomial polynomials are linearly independent.

What it serves. A structure theorem ('dévissage') for ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules over a PID:
- every such object is a sum of the indecomposables Λ^iL, L(i,n), Λ^jΨ;
- it is classified by its homology plus the eventual Hilbert polynomial.

The next page then characterizes flasque/projective objects (only Λ^iL summands). It reduces the description of the whole additive category to computing Hom between these indecomposables.
errors: In the rank formula the second sum is written Σ_{0≤j≤n} ν_j C(n,i); it must be C(n,j) (index slip). The same slip occurs in the polynomial at the bottom of the page.
'rg H_j(L(i,n)) = k/div n' conflates rank with the module itself. H_{i-1} = k/(n) is torsion, of rank 0; what is meant is H_j itself.

Degree conventions drift: the complex is drawn in degrees i, i+1, yet the homology is placed in degree i-1. The bottom polynomial uses C(n,i) for i ≥ 1 where C(n+1,i) appears above. These are harmless at the level of eventual polynomials but inconsistent.

Iso-class determination needs the actual elementary divisors of tors H_i, not just their number ρ_{i+1}. Read with 'H_i(L.)' fully known, the claim is fine; read with only ranks and counts, it is not.

ideas.what: Indecomposable semi-simplicial modules L(i,n) realizing the elementary-divisor block k --n--> k, as an extension of Λ^iΨ by Λ^{i-1}Ψ whose connecting map is multiplication by n.
ideas.modern_name: Indecomposable objects / Krull–Schmidt decomposition for perfect modules over the semi-simplicial category Δ_inj (Δ-modules)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard reference known; related to Dold–Kan-type theorems (Dold, Kan 1958; Pirashvili for Γ-modules 2000)

ideas.what: Hilbert function of a ∂-perfect semi-simplicial module is eventually a sum of binomial polynomials C(m+1,i), C(m,j), with coefficients given by multiplicities of indecomposables.
ideas.modern_name: Eventual polynomiality of dimension growth for representations of combinatorial categories (cf. FI-modules / Sam–Snowden Gröbner methods)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Church–Ellenberg–Farb (FI-modules, 2012-15); Sam–Snowden (2017) for general combinatorial categories

ideas.what: Classification theorem: a ∂-perfect semi-simplicial module over a PID is determined up to iso by its homology (ranks + torsion divisors) and its eventual Hilbert polynomial.
ideas.modern_name: Complete invariants for perfect Δ_inj-modules over a PID

ideas.what: Computing homology of L(i,n) via the long exact sequence of the extension.

missed.claim: An explicit structure/classification theorem for ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules over a principal ring. Indecomposables are Λ^iL, Λ^jΨ, L(i,n); complete invariants are homology plus the eventual Hilbert polynomial. I know of no published counterpart.
missed.quote: Donc L. est connue à isom. près quand on connaît a) rg H_i(L.) = ν_i et le nombre ρ_{i+1} de ses diviseurs de torsion ... et b) la fonction f_L pour n grand
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Semi-simplicial (Δ_inj) modules are representations of a combinatorial category, a setting now studied intensively. A Krull–Schmidt classification with explicit indecomposables is the kind of result sought there.

missed.claim: Grothendieck ties eventual polynomiality of ranks of semi-simplicial modules to homological invariants via exterior powers of the standard module. This anticipates themes of representation stability (FI-modules, polynomial Hilbert functions) for the category of finite ordinals with injections.
missed.quote: La fonction de Hilbert des L(i,n) est donc la même que celle de Λ^iL, savoir C(n+1,i)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests an explicit description of 'Hilbert series' of Δ_inj-modules in terms of homology. This could be compared with Sam–Snowden-style results and with Koszul-type resolutions over OI/FI.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, apparently unpublished classification of perfect semi-simplicial modules over a PID, with explicit indecomposables and Hilbert-polynomial invariants. The individual steps are elementary, and the result is a natural Dold–Kan-adjacent exercise.
transcription_corrections: 'h --n--> k' and 'k → h' should read 'k --n--> k' and 'k → k' (h is a misread k).
'cette extension k → k (cf ...) est nulle' likely reads 'l'homom. associé k → k (cf ...) est n·id', since the computed H_{i-1} = k/(n) requires multiplication by n.
'La fonction de Hilbert des L[?]' is 'des L(i,n)'.
'Donc H/L.' is likely 'Donc L.' (L is known up to isomorphism).
'par quand on connaît' should be 'dès qu'on connaît' or 'quand on connaît'.
Circled insertion: '∂-parfait, il est connu à isom. près'.
